title: Android 17 QPR1 lands with useful upgrades all over the place
summary: Google has been busy tinkering with just about everything.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out with a sweeping range of smaller upgrades and refinements. Some features will already look familiar from earlier betas, while others are new to the wider release. There are changes across everything from Digital Wellbeing and multitasking to media controls, security, and general UI polish. Android 17 has been stable for a few months, and after no fewer than nine beta versions, Google is rolling out its first meaty update. The first Quarterly Platform Release doesn’t bring one game-changing feature that’ll transform how you use your phone, but it makes a surprising number of smaller changes across customization, multitasking, media, Digital Wellbeing, and more. Android 17 QPR1 has a lot to unpack, and we’ll navigate you through it. In a detailed Reddit post , Google’s Mishaal Rahman outlined what’s changing with the release. Google says QPR1 is rolling out to Pixel devices first, while the additions are now part of the wider Android platform and could therefore show up in updates from other manufacturers later. If you’ve followed the Android 17 betas closely, or own a Pixel 11, some of this will look famili…

title: Bruce Springsteen Wins Appeal, Won’t Face Lawsuit Over Vintage Car on 2022 Album Cover
summary: An appellate court upheld the dismissal of litigation over the album artwork for Only The Strong Survive.
body: Bruce Springsteen has defeated a second attempt at litigation over his use of a New Jersey man’s 1967 Pontiac GTO in the album art for his 2022 cover collection Only the Strong Survive. In a Tuesday (Sept. 15) ruling, obtained by Billboard , a New Jersey appeals court affirmed the earlier dismissal of a lawsuit brought against Springsteen by the family of deceased classic car collector Louis Billotti. The case had also targeted Sony Music, which owns Springsteen’s label Columbia Records, and his longtime manager Jon Landau . title: Samsung’s upcoming clip-on Galaxy Buds swing by the FCC
summary: The Galaxy Buds Able (or Galaxy Buds On) could be announced any time.
body: TL;DR A new pair of earbuds from Samsung has appeared in FCC documentation. All signs point to the newly authorized buds being Samsung’s first pair of clip-on earbuds. This lines up neatly with a previous report stating the earbuds could launch this month or next. We’ve been tracking developments around a pair of unannounced earbuds from Samsung, internally referred to in Samsung’s software as “able,” since April . The earbuds, which could come to market under the name Galaxy Buds On , might be announced any time now: a device with a model number matching the upcoming earbuds has just appeared in FCC documents. The FCC documentation shows that a Bluetooth headset from Samsung with the model number SMU600 was granted equipment authorization today, September 15. The grant means Samsung is now clear to market the earbuds in the US.

summary: Google widens Scam Detection's to multiple countries, but saves the best bit for the US.
body: Credit: Brady Snyder / Android Authority TL;DR Google has released the September Pixel Drop with new Scam Detection features for its phones. The update expands the availability of Scam Detection in Google Messages to many more regions. Scam Detection now also works in third-party apps through Gboard, but this feature is limited to the US for now. After revealing a host of new features for a broad range of Android devices earlier this month, Samsung is now giving Pixel users new features. Beyond the new features in the latest September Pixel Drop , Google is expanding some existing features into new territories. One such feature is Scam Detection in Google Messages , which is now available in a host of countries and languages. Google has confirmed that alongside the US, Pixel’s Scam Detection in Google Messages is now available in Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, and the UK. In addition to English, Pixel devices will be able to detect seemingly suspicious or rogue messages in Arabic, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese, and Spanish.

title: Google Translate is getting a major offline upgrade
summary: Offline Live Translate finally arrives, but only for newer Pixels.
body: TL;DR Live Translate lets you directly talk to speakers of other languages, but so far has required a data connection. Google Translate is now adding offline Live support. Conversations are supported between English and French, German, Portuguese, Italian, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Russian, and Swedish. Our phones are fantastic tools for helping us deal with unfamiliar situations, but all too often that requires having an active data connection — which can be far from a certainty, depending on where we’re going. That’s exactly why it’s so important to have offline options for some of those most critical tools, like offline support in Google Maps . Earlier this year we spotted Google working towards another new offline mode, as it prepared support for Live Translate without a data connection . And now we’re finally starting to see it arrive. When we last took a peek at Googles in-development efforts back in May, it appeared that we could expect offline Live Translate support for at least English, French, German, Portuguese, Italian, and Spanish.

title: Looks like Samsung Gallery has already found its OneDrive replacement
summary: Surprise, you're using Google Photos.
body: TL;DR Samsung is ending a partnership with Microsoft that saw images backed up from Samsung Gallery stored in OneDrive. OneDrive will instead back up photos to Google’s cloud storage in the future. Images stored this way will be accessible in both Samsung Gallery and Google Photos. Samsung announced earlier this year that it would stop working with Microsoft OneDrive to store user images and videos in the cloud. That partnership is officially ending at the end of September , and preparations for nixing the functionality have already begun. Now that Microsoft is on its way out, we’ve learned Samsung will partner with Google for cloud storage going forward. As spotted by X user Sandeep Adap , a new version of Samsung’s Gallery Cloud Sync service has popped up on the Galaxy Store. The service’s description specifies that it backs up photos and videos in Google Cloud.

summary: Spotify's algorithm can now ignore all those nursery rhymes your kids have been using your account for.
body: TL;DR Spotify is rolling out a new setting that lets parents stop kids’ and family music from influencing their recommendations. Turning it off keeps children’s music out of features like Discover Weekly, Daily Mix, and even 2026 Wrapped. The change works retroactively and is available globally on mobile for both Free and Premium users. After a successful pilot launch, Spotify’s Managed Accounts made their way to all US-based users earlier this summer, allowing parents to give their kids their own space on Spotify, all while maintaining control over their listening environment and habits. However, even when kids have access to their own space on Spotify, there are bound to be moments, like car rides, when you inevitably end up playing their music from your own account. title: This global Android bestseller gets a successor with a bigger battery
summary: The Galaxy A08 4G keeps most of what worked while fixing two key weaknesses.
body: TL;DR Samsung has quietly launched the Galaxy A08 4G, successor to the Galaxy A07 4G, one of 2026’s best-selling Android phones. The biggest upgrades are a larger 6,000mAh battery, improved IP64 protection, and Android 17 with One UI 9 out of the box. Most other hardware stays familiar, while Samsung promises six Android OS upgrades and security support through September 2032. The Galaxy A07 4G has had the kind of year most budget phones can only dream of. It finished Q1 2026 as the world’s best-selling Android phone , ranking fourth overall, and was still the second-highest Android model in Q2 after the Galaxy S26 Ultra took the Android sales crown. Those are massive shoes to fill, and Samsung is now sending in the Galaxy A08 4G with targeted upgrades rather than a full overhaul. Samsung has quietly listed the Galaxy A08 4G on its official website in Bosnia and Herzegovina (spotted via SamMobile ), revealing a phone that looks familiar on paper. The biggest change is the battery, which grows from 5,000mAh on the A07 to 6,000mAh. Samsung has also raised dust and water resistance from IP54 to IP64, giving the new model better dust protection while retaining splash resistance.

title: Your Android phone is hiding your headphones’ best audio quality — here’s how to unlock it
summary: Android hides a world of Bluetooth codecs. Here's what they do and which matter.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Your Android phone might be capable of far more Bluetooth audio options than you think. You see, most of the time, Android’s Bluetooth audio menu exposes only a small fraction of what your phone and headphones can actually do. For more advanced settings, you may need to reach for your headphones’ companion app or dive into Android’s Developer Settings , where a much wider selection of Bluetooth codecs and playback modes is available. Take my aging Sony WH-1000XM3, for example. It technically supports Qualcomm’s aptX, yet my phone’s regular Bluetooth settings only offer LDAC as the high-definition option and SBC for standard playback. Some phones don’t even expose an HD codec option at all.

title: Gemini overlay crowding your phone screen? This nifty gesture could soon come to your rescue
summary: Gemini could soon duck out of your way while it works in the background.
body: Credit: AssembleDebug / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing a new gesture to minimize Gemini overlays into a bubble. Doing so keeps the chat running in the background without keeping you from using the phone. The gesture requires you to swipe left or right on the overlay to minimize it. Google has been working to make Gemini more useful, even when it’s running in the background. A few months ago, we learned it was testing new ways to let Gemini work without hogging space at the top of the screen, plus the option to offload tasks to Spark even without opening the app fully, which was spotted recently. Now, we’re seeing more behind-the-scenes work to make Gemini work offstage. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: 5 features the iPhone Duo shamelessly copied from Android foldables
summary: Eight years of very careful note-taking.
body: It’s been more than eight years since Samsung kicked off the foldable phone era, and a lot has happened since. Motorola, Google, OnePlus, Xiaomi, vivo, OPPO — you name it — almost everyone has had a go at making a foldable. Apple, meanwhile, has spent all these years sitting on the sidelines. But then again, that’s very Apple; it rarely wants to be first. It would rather wait, watch everyone else figure things out, and eventually show up with its own take. And after seeing the iPhone Duo for the first time, it feels like Apple was taking notes the entire time. Credit where it’s due, because there’s a lot here that I already love. The Duo looks ridiculously compact and adorable, a lot like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . The software optimization Apple showed during the event impressed me, and that barely-there display crease might be one of its biggest wins.

title: YouTube fixes the login issue that kept viewers off their TVs and consoles
summary: Some users couldn’t even watch as guests.
body: TL;DR A YouTube login issue signed some users out on TVs and gaming consoles, while others couldn’t even watch as guests. YouTube says the issue is fully fixed, so affected users should be able to sign in and watch again. YouTube has spent the past couple of weeks making its TV app easier to use. A new companion experience lets your phone handle searches and comments while the video keeps playing on the TV, and account lock adds privacy to shared TVs. That progress didn’t help viewers who got home, opened YouTube, and found themselves signed out. Some couldn’t even watch as guests. Luckily, that’s now been fixed. In a community update , YouTube says it investigated reports of trouble signing into its app on living room devices and resolved the issue. The company says viewers should no longer encounter login errors. But it hasn’t explained what caused the disruption or whether it’s linked to recent app updates.

The feature is designed to reduce motion sickness by displaying small dots on the edge of your screen that move in real time to help synchronize what your eyes see and your body feels while riding in a vehicle. Motion Assist requires Android 17 or higher to render the dots across all system surfaces. Motion sickness is a very common condition. While some people are more susceptible to it than others, enough motion can get anyone feeling a little green. Google recently released a new feature for Pixel owners called Motion Assist to help combat motion sickness . Now, that feature is spreading to more Android devices. According to Google’s Mishaal Rahman , Android’s Motion Assist feature is now rolling out beyond Pixel phones. So, if you’re a passenger in a moving vehicle, you can now turn this feature on to help reduce the likelihood of getting motion sick. The feature requires Android 17 or higher to render the dots across all system surfaces.

title: Gemini on your Google Home talking to itself? A fix is on the way
summary: Gemini can mistake its own voice for yours, triggering loops and duplicate commands.
body: TL;DR Gemini Live can hear its own voice on some Google Home devices, causing it to interrupt itself and get stuck in a loop. Users have reported crashes, repeated responses, and Gemini creating duplicate timers after hearing its own confirmation. Google has acknowledged the bug and is rolling out improvements, although it hasn’t provided a completion timeline. Earlier this year, some Android Auto users watched Gemini Live hear its own voice and spiral into a conversation with itself. In-car audio setups emerged as a possible culprit, but similar behavior is now surfacing on some Google Home devices. The good news? Google has now acknowledged the bug and says improvements are rolling out. The issue surfaced on Reddit after a Google Home user said Gemini Live had become unusable. Responding last Friday, the official Google Nest Community account confirmed that Live Mode was interrupting itself on some devices and said improvements were rolling out.

The unusual increase would arrive nearly seven months after the phones launched, amid soaring RAM and component costs. Samsung says it is reviewing its pricing but has made no final decision, with no indication of a US increase. When Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max , higher prices than last year’s models felt inevitable. But few expected Apple to use the launch to raise prices on its older iPhones . Now, Android’s biggest name may be reading from the same playbook, as a Korean outlet claims Samsung is considering an unusual post-launch price hike for the Galaxy S26 series. According to Hans Economy , a South Korean carrier has informed retailers that wholesale prices for every Galaxy S26 model will rise by 149,600 won (about $110) on October 1. That would be unusual because Samsung launched the phones in March, putting the alleged price hike nearly seven months into their life cycle.

title: Apple’s Handoff lets two iPhones share one number, but it won’t come cheap
summary: T-Mobile will put your number on a second iPhone, but for the right price.
body: TL;DR Apple’s new Handoff feature, which lets you use the same number on two iPhones, won’t be free. T-Mobile, the only carrier to support Handoff at launch, will cost an extra $5 per month. T-Mobile says both phones should be able to use crucial features like calling, SMS, data, and even T-Satellite. The iPhone 18 Pro , which Apple announced last week, lacks any significant upgrade other than its new chip. Even the new camera Apple touted adds a feature Android brands have had for years . Irrespective of that, something that makes the iPhone 18 Pro truly compelling is the ability to use another iPhone with the same phone number, much like you would with an Apple Watch. This feature is called “Handoff, ” and it currently requires carrier support. That means only a handful of carriers will initially support it and may charge you more for the service, especially as they’re giving you the opportunity to sell you another line. At launch, T-Mobile is the only carrier in the US to support Handoff, while Verizon is likely to add support in the coming months.
